newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss money market rates little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss money market rates little changed.

text.p: Swiss money market rates were little changed with tomorrow/next money quoted at 1-3/8 to 1-1/2 percent.
The Swiss National bank was seen adding liquidity in its routine morning market operations. Traders said it put money into the market at a rate of 1-1/2 percent for two weeks, from September 24.
Traders said uncertainty surrounding Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health increased safe-have demand for Swiss francs and also affected the money market.

There was no discernible reaction to news the SNB's M0 base showed a faster growth rate in August, rising by a seasonally adjusted 4.3 percent versus the fourth quarter of 1995. In August, the SNB had reported M0 grew in July by a seasonally adjusted 3.0 percent versus the fourth quarter.
On an adjusted annual basis, M0 grew 5.7 percent in August.
This compared with 4.5 percent annually for July, according to the SNB's August report.
